title: Output-polynomial hypergraph transversal enumeration
formal: Do there exist one deterministic Turing algorithm A and constants \(C,c>0\) which, for every finite hypergraph H, output all its inclusion-minimal transversals exactly once, terminate, and use at most \(C(\mathrm{L}(H)+\mathrm{L}_{\mathrm{out}}(H)+1)^{c}\) steps?
context: Paraphrase of a question in Enumeration Complexity: Incremental Time, Delay and Space (2021), §7.1, unnumbered transversal problem. The exact definitions, parameters and assumptions must be read at the cited location. This short draft has not been developed into a self-contained research card.

definitions: \(H=([n],E), n\ge 0\), is supplied as the explicit vertex list and a finite list of edges \(e\subseteq [n]\), each edge an increasing list of binary vertex identifiers. Repeated edges have no effect. \(\mathrm{L}(H)\) is the bit length of this input including delimiters. A transversal is a set \(T\subseteq [n]\) intersecting every \(e\in E\); it is inclusion-minimal when no proper subset has this property. Output each such T as an increasing list of its binary vertex identifiers with a delimiter, in arbitrary order; no duplicate, nonminimal or incomplete output is allowed. \(\mathrm{L}_{\mathrm{out}}(H)\) is the sum of the bit lengths of these records, counting one delimiter even for \(T=\varnothing\). If E is empty, the unique minimal transversal is \(\varnothing\). If E contains \(\varnothing\), there is no transversal and \(\mathrm{L}_{\mathrm{out}}=0\). Time includes all computation, output and termination detection. The polynomial and algorithm are independent of n, E, edge size and output size; there is no separate delay or workspace bound, advice, oracle or randomization. In this statement, “explicitly given/encoded/listed” means the entire finite list, table or syntax tree described above is part of the input or output, with its full encoding counted; it does not mean a circuit, oracle or program generating a larger object.

sentences: A hypergraph transversal meets every hyperedge, and it is minimal when no selected vertex can be removed while preserving that property.
The question asks to enumerate all minimal transversals in time polynomial in the combined input and output size.
The family can be exponentially large, so output-polynomial time is the relevant total-work target.
The challenge is finding every minimal hitting set without spending disproportionate time on nonminimal candidates or repeated discoveries.
This is a central enumeration problem linking dual hypergraph descriptions, and the source's explicit input model should be preserved when comparing it with restricted hypergraph classes.
